name: Acoustic, Clear
description: The earlier voicing, whose bands keep their width as they rise: the high-pass at 80 Hz, the low middle cut gently at 200 Hz, the high middle up wide at 5 kHz, and a high shelf for sparkle.

name: Bass, Even
description: A low shelf up a little at 80 Hz, the low middle cut at 250 Hz where a bass gets muddy, the high middle up at 1.2 kHz for the strings, and the compressor at 4 to 1 with a slow release so the notes come out even.

name: Drum Bus, Sidechain
description: The high-pass at 150 Hz moved into the compressor's sidechain, so the kick does not pump the kit, and the compressor at 3 to 1 with a slower attack for punch; the bands lift the low end and the top.

name: Electric, Bite
description: Both filters closing in, at 100 Hz and 9 kHz, the high middle up and narrow at 2 kHz for bite, and a little cut at 500 Hz, so a distorted guitar sits under a vocal.

name: Kick, Knock
description: The low band as a bell at 60 Hz for weight, a narrow cut at 400 Hz for the box, the high middle up at 3 kHz for the beater, and the gate shutting the kick's spill between hits with a quick release.

name: Room, Squash
description: The compressor as a limiter, its threshold low and its release quick, on drum room microphones: the room pumps and the tails come up. Low and high shelves lift what the squash dulls.

name: Snare, Crack
description: The high-pass at 100 Hz, the low middle up at 220 Hz for body, the high middle up at 5 kHz for crack, the expander taking the spill down by 12 dB, and the compressor fast and firm.

name: Vocal, Up Front
description: The high-pass at 90 Hz, the low middle cut a little and wide at 300 Hz against boxiness, the high middle up at 3.5 kHz, a high shelf for air, and the compressor at 4 to 1 after the equaliser with the fast attack, so the lifted consonants are held too. The automatic make-up keeps the level.
